answer: Behavioral fingerprint spanning. Each agent's action sequence is hashed against timing and ordering, and any near-duplicate trace triggers a mandatory challenge like sand sifting across a dune, revealing copied behavior. Duplicated identities must then sustain distinct interaction histories, an ocean of ongoing compute and attention cost per clone. A public commit-reveal log acts as a mirror: an attacker reusing patterns sees every clone's overlap instantly, forfeiting the registration deposit plus accumulated reputation.
